articleTitle: SAE Network: A Deep Learning Method for Traffic Flow Prediction
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Traffic flow forecasting is one of the most important work of the intelligent transport system (ITS). It has extensive and promising applications to improve the traffic conditions. However, the forecasting accuracy may not be high enough for traffic control considering high-dynamic change and various disturbance in the real world. In order to improve the forecasting accuracy, huge amount of historical traffic data are studied. In this paper, four months of aggregated traffic flow data via vehicle detector on a city ring way are obtained and selected for further analysis. An improved stacked autoencoder (SAE)model based on deep learning network is proposed to extract the features among traffic flow data. This predict model is trained in a greedy layer-wise method. The prediction results illustrate that this proposed model with higher accuracy is superior to other methods for traffic flow prediction.

articleTitle: Attitude Tracking for a Quadrotor UAV Based on Fuzzy PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Recently, quadrotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become one of the most interesting fields of research. Attitude control is a crucial research point and is also an important basis for the stable flight of the UAV. Therefore, it is necessary and meaningful to study the attitude tracking problem of the quadrotor UAV. Firstly, the control principle of the quadrotor UAV is described in the paper. Subsequently, the mathematical dynamic model of UAV is introduced via some basic derivation. Secondly, the overall control structure of the UAV is presented. In order to improve control performance, the fuzzy controller is used to tune the three parameters of the proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller in altitude channel and attitude channel. In addition, the realization of the proposed control algorithm for the quadrotor UAV is presented in detail. Finally, the simulation test about the altitude and attitude tracking of the UAV is completed in Matlab/Simulink using PID controller and fuzzy PID controller respectively. Experimental results show that PID coupled with fuzzy control has a better tracking performance than pure PID.

articleTitle: An Amplitudes-Perturbation Data Augmentation Method in Convolutional Neural Networks for EEG Decoding
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Brain-Computer Interface (BCI)system provides a pathway between humans and the outside world by analyzing brain signals which contain potential neural information. Electroencephalography (EEG)is one of most commonly used brain signals and EEG recognition is an important part of BCI system. Recently, convolutional neural networks (ConvNet)in deep learning are becoming the new cutting edge tools to tackle the problem of EEG recognition. However, training an effective deep learning model requires a big number of data, which limits the application of EEG datasets with a small number of samples. In order to solve the issue of data insufficiency in deep learning for EEG decoding, we propose a novel data augmentation method that add perturbations to amplitudes of EEG signals after transform them to frequency domain. In experiments, we explore the performance of signal recognition with the state-of-the-art models before and after data augmentation on BCI Competition IV dataset 2a and our local dataset. The results show that our data augmentation technique can improve the accuracy of EEG recognition effectively.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of High-Speed Railway Bogies Based on LSTM
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The bogie abnormal state is usually reflected in the abnormal vibration of railway bogie. According to the different functions and performance degradation degree of the mechanical components in entire railway system, the abnormal vibration signal is reflected in different ways. This paper presents a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)model to analyze the vibration signal that has a deeply excavated internal correlation, since the bogie vibration data are time series data, the use of recurrent neural network (RNN)can extract internal information embedded in the bogie vibration signal well. LSTM network that is able to control the amount of data in input, memory, and output is an upgrade of RNN, the previous data and the future data are connected to analyze the characteristics of the current data by LSTM. And the accuracy rate of this model for multi-fault classification reaches 94 %.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Systems with Time-Varying Delays Using Bessel-Legendre Inequalities
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of delay-dependent stability of linear systems with time-varying delays. Firstly, a new free-matrix-based inequality is proposed, which is an improved version of Bessel-Legendre inequality. This inequality is applicable to time-varying-delay systems. It overcome the drawback the resulting bounds inevitably include the reciprocal convexity when employing the Bessel-Legendre inequality to deal with time-varying-delay systems. Based on the novel inequality proposed and by constructing an appropriate Lyapunov- Krasovskii functional (LKF), improved stability criteria are presented in a sets of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Numerical examples suggest that the results outperform the state of the art in the literature.

articleTitle: Matched Filtering and Orthogonal Matching Pursuit for Terahertz Coded-Aperture Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Terahertz coded-aperture imaging (TCAI) adopts re coded-aperture to produce spatiotemporal independent signals, in which way TCAI can achieve high-resolution, forward-looking and staring imaging. However, it is difficult to reconstruct the sparsity-driven target while the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is too low, which makes the back-signal vector and reference-signal matrix cannot match each other. Therefore, matching filtering and orthogonal matching pursuit (MF -OMP) approach is proposed. First, the range profile is obtained by mathed-filtering pulse compression, and the range cells containing the scatterers are extracted to formulate the dictionary. Then, the azimuth and pitching reconstructions are processed by OMP. The proposed approach can enhance the SNR. The effectiveness of the MF-OMP is verified by numerous simulations.

Author Keywords: matched filtering and orthogonal matching pursuit (MF-OMP)

articleTitle: Containment Control for Fuzzy Multi-Agent Systems Subject to Stochastic Controller Gain Variation
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper studies the containment control problem for a kind of nonlinear discrete-time multi-agent systems (MASs)with stochastic controller gain variation. More specifically, the nonlinear dynamics of MASs are modeled by the discrete-time Takagi-Sugeno (T-S)fuzzy systems, which can approximate many practical nonlinear systems in reality. Firstly, by introducing a stochastic variable and an uncertain term in the control protocol, a stochastic uncertain closed-loop system is derived that captures the stochastic controller gain variation phenomenon. By means of the Lyapunov stability theory and linear matrix inequality (LMI)technique, a novel sufficient condition is obtained such that containment control for such a kind of nonlinear systems is achieved. Then, after some matrices manipulation, the controller gains are calculated by solving some LMIs. A numerical study is finally proposed for the validation of the controller design.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Observer(SMO)Based Adaptive Backstepping Control for a Multi-Vectored Propeller Airship[1]
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper proposes a path following method for a sensorless(assume the angular velocity and velocity sensors are destroyed)airship (which has four vectored thrusts)by using SMO-based adaptive backstepping approach. Firstly, the nonlinear dynamics and kinematics model are introduced. Regard the aerodynamic coefficient vector as the system uncertainty, a SMO is proposed to estimate the airship's (angular)velocity based on the above-mentioned models. Then, a path following controller is designed, which consists of two modules: an adaptive-based module and a backstepping control module. The adaptive-based module is used to estimate the uncertainty of the system, while the backstepping control module calculates a control law to realize the path following. Simulation results for the multi-vectored propeller airship are carried out to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stacking Objects Picking System Based on Structured Light
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for stacking objects picking system that combines two-dimensional vision and three-dimensional vision. Structured light method is used to acquire three-dimensional information. Based on the information, the region of interest is extracted. A Generalized Hough Transform method is then used to match object and estimate the pose of object. Finally, the pose of the object is sent to the manipulator for automatic picking. The method proposed in this paper is very effective for the capture of stacking flat objects. The combination of two-dimensional and three-dimensional methods improves the efficiency of the algorithm. The experiments show that the system has high performance.

articleTitle: Long-Term Forecasting of Time Series Based on Sliding Window Information Granules and Fuzzy Inference System
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new granular time series approach based on sliding window information granules and fuzzy inference system for predicting long-term uncertain data sets. The sliding window information granules, which extract and choose more and useful temporal segments from the initial time series, can capture more essential relationships. And fuzzy inference system based on weighted average is used to predict the future segment window. The experimental results illustrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-Motor Synchronous Servo System Control Based on Improved Inertia Identification
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In view of the influence of load inertia variation on the control performance of multi-motor synchronous servo system when multiple rocket launchers launch continuously, the load inertia identification method for multi-motor synchronous servo system is studied in this paper. In order to solve the problem of data saturation in the identification process, the least square identification method with forgetting factor is introduced. In view of the shortage of fixed forgetting factor, a variable forgetting factor formula based on error is proposed, which makes the improved algorithm more suitable for the application of multi-motor servo system. Finally, the accuracy of the proposed identification algorithm in multi-motor synchronous control system is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: High-Precision Tracking of Piezoelectric Actuator Using Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Piezoelectric Actuators (PEAs)are the crucial constituent components in high precision motion control of piezoelectric nano-positioning systems. However, its control precision is seriously restricted by the intrinsic rate-dependent hysteretic nonlinear characteristic. In this paper, by modeling PEA in a second-order disturbance-based structure, a novel active disturbance rejection control (ADRC)strategy is proposed to settle hysteresis compensation for tracking control of PEAs. Different from the prevailing direct model inversion method, which extremely depends on the precision of the detailed mathematical model of rate-dependent hysteresis, the proposed control methodology is model-free whereby hysteretic nonlinearity is treated as disturbance and rejected. Comparative experiments including extra tests using pure proportional-integral (PI)control without model inverse hysteresis compensation are implemented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method on a PEA for 3 different types of signals. The promising experiment results manifest that the proposed ADRC scheme is better than pure PI control scheme in terms of control precision and tracking errors.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Image Classification Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The deep learning is of great interest recently. MIT Technology Review ranked deep learning as the top 10 technology breakthrough in 2013. The multi-layered structure of Deep Learning Network enables it to learn deeper features of data and improve the accuracy of data identification and classification. Hyperspectral image classification technology is the most important research direction in hyperspectral remote sensing, and has been widely used in military and civil fields. It has become a trend to apply deep learning to hyperspectral image classification. But deep learning is data-driven and requires a lot of data, however, the hyperspectral data we deal with is a small data set. In the classification of small data sets, compared to the traditional classification methods, classification of the deep learning is more effective. In this paper, we study the convolution neural network which is excellent in the field of image processing, and compare the effect of hyperspectral image classification with the traditional Classification method.

articleTitle: Research on Torque Ripple and its Minimization Method of Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: To solve the severe torque ripple problem of switched reluctance motor(SRM), this paper firstly analyzes the causes of torque ripple of SRM and measures the torque ripple waveform by experiment, and then proposes one torque ripple minimization of SRM based on peak-valley complementary principle method. Two sets of motor subsystems with the same stator and rotor parameters are used to generate two symmetrical torque ripple waveform whose electrical degrees of phase difference is 180. Based on this method, the superposition of these two torque ripple outputting to the load can offset the torque ripple of SRM. Accordingly, this paper also proposes a design scheme of SRM body, which the two sets of SRMs are embedded into one integral motor system. In this motor system, the two sets of stator pole positions are the same, while the rotor pole positions are shifted by a certain angle to obtain the torque ripple waveforms with a phase difference of 180 degrees, at the same time the two SRMs need to have the same direction, speed and power to run. Finally, the practicability and effectiveness of the above-mentioned method can be verified through the simulink simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Research on Interaction Safety of Human-Robot Collision Based on Series Elastic Actuator
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: How to ensure interaction safety between human and robot is one of the key problems of human-robot harmony. As a typical flexible actuator, series elastic actuator (SEA)is gradually used in interactive manipulator. However, research on human-robot interaction safety of manipulator based on SEA is quite in lack. Aimed at interaction safety of SEA during collision, single-DOF SEA experimental platform was designed and explored the influence to collision force of soft covering thickness, load inertia, collision velocity and joint stiffness. The results show that, increasing soft covering thickness, decreasing load inertia, collision velocity and joint stiffness can diminish collision force. The results of experiments can be conducted to design the interactive manipulator with multi-degrees.

articleTitle: Enhanced Quantum Neural Network Integrated in Health State Estimation for Aircraft Fuel System
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: As the core part of the airplane, aircraft fuel system has attracted much attention due to ever increasing demand on the enhancement of safety and reliability. In order to guarantee the flight safety and achieve condition based maintenance, the health states of aircraft fuel system should be estimated accurately. This paper illustrates the working principle and the core components of aircraft fuel system. A performance degradation model of aircraft fuel system is built based on the erosion of the boost pump. In this paper, an enhanced quantum neural network (EQNN)is developed to estimate the health state. The basic quantum neural network (QNN)has an inherently excellent capability for classification problem with overlapping boundary. In order to improve the performance, the loss function of the QNN is redesigned. Finally, EQNN is applied to estimate the health state of the aircraft fuel system. For validating of the performance of the proposed method, the proposed method is compared with other two classic neural networks.

articleTitle: Adaptive Critic Optimal Fuzzy Control for Quarter-Car Suspension Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: For quarter car suspension systems with uncertain mass, first Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy model is constructed by using sector nonlinear. Based on adaptive critic technology and zero-sum game theory, an online adaptive fuzzy optimal control method is studied. A critic fuzzy logic system is given to approximate the solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation with H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub>-cost function in an on-line way, instead of traditional action-critic architecture. A simulation example is employed to illustrate the validity of the scheme of the paper.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Controller Design for Vehicle Active Suspensions Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The study concerns the problem of fuzzy controller design for vehicle active suspensions based on genetic algorithm (GA). Three performance requirements, i.e. ride comfort, good road-holding ability and suspension stroke limitation are considered simultaneously in the controller design process. GA is employed to optimize the parameters of membership functions and fuzzy control rules to obtain better control performance. Simulation and discussions are presented to demonstrate the validity of the designed fuzzy controller.

articleTitle: Recursive Sliding Mode Based Iterative Learning Control
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel adaptive iterative learning control scheme is proposed to cope with the output tracking problem for a class of nonlinear plants with unknown parameters in the condition of arbitrary initial error. Lyapunov synthesis is utilized to design the iterative learning controller. The initial rectifying action and the recursive terminal sliding mode technique are integratedly employed to overcome initial nonzero error. As the number of iteration increases, the rectified signal converges to zero over the whole time interval, such that system output may precisely track the reference signal during the pre-specified part interval.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Based Expression Classification with Face Alignment
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs)have been proved to be excellent in image classification including facial expression recognition. However, CNNs commonly fail to learn the key expression characteristics with different facial angles. In this paper, the facial expression recognition problem is considered. The facial alignment technology is employed to adjust the inclined faces where an affine transformation is utilized such that the faces lie on a horizontal line. Then, in consideration of the scale of the model parameters, a sequential CNN is designed to extract the facial features, where a global averaged pooling layer is adopted instead of the fully connected layer. Comparing with the data augmentation, the experimental results on the three benchmark datasets (ie., Jaffe, CK+ and FER-2013)show that better performance is guaranteed by our model with less adjustable parameters.

articleTitle: Application of Electrical Capacitance Tomography in Pneumatic Conveying of Pulverized Coal
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: On-line detection of pulverized coal concentration, speed and the mass flow are of great importance for safety, environmental protection and energy conservation in industry of power plant boiler, which is also a hot spot research for boiler study. This paper introduces the application of electrical capacitance tomography in pneumatic conveying of pulverized coal. An 8-electrode ECT system including both hardware and software is developed. The hardware of this ECT system consists of sensors optimization, small capacitance measurement circuit, data acquisition control module based on DSP. AC-based capacitance measuring circuits is adopted in this paper which have advantages of high speed response, stray-immune, low drifting, etc. Software of imaging reconstruction computer is described. This ECT system has been designed on modularization configuration to be conveniently used in industry field. Moreover, the signal long-distance transfer, imaging speed and the problems in practical industry applications are considered.

articleTitle: Quadrator QFT Control Based on Model Reduction Method
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, we study the quadrotor model reduction method based on balanced truncation and its QFT control problem. Due to the under-actuation characteristics of the quadrotor, the controller design is simplified from the perspective of the actual physical system, and the actual design parameters are used to verify the performance of the controller. In this paper, QFT method is used to transform the control problem of MIMO system into MISO control problem and design related controllers. Finally, the reduced-order system with QFT controller is verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Guaranteed Cost Control for a Class of Discrete-Time Systems with Saturation Nonlinearities
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: For a class of discrete-time systems with saturation nonlinearities, the design problem of the optimal guaranteed cost state feedback controller is formulated in this paper. Together with a given quadratic cost index, a sufficient condition for the existence of state feedback guaranteed cost controller is derived by the means of Lyapunov stability theory and linear matrix inequalities(LMI). Furthermore, a LMI based new criterion that the optimal guaranteed cost control problem of state feedback control law is proposed. Finally, a numerical example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: RBF Neural Network Adaptive PID Control for Energy Storage System in Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In photovoltaic microgrid, the output power of PV array will change with the change of external light and temperature. In order to maintain the stability of output power of PV system, energy storage system is usually added into the system. In a energy storage system, the most widely used control method is proportional-integral-derivative (PID)based control, however, the control effect of PID control is dependent on parameter tuning. In this paper, a PID controller based on adaptive radial basis function (RBF)neural network is proposed to adjust the PID parameters adaptively, and improve the response speed, anti-interference ability and robustness of the traditional PID controller. In the end, the energy storage system is built in the MATLAB/Simulink software, which is applied to the 100kW photovoltaic array to stabilize the output power when the light and temperature changed.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Control of Damping Force in the Air Suspension System
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The performance of the electronically controlled air suspension is an important factor to determine the handling stability and ride comfort of the vehicle. Damping force is one of the main output variables in the air suspension system, which is used to coordinate the free oscillation of air spring. In this paper, a fuzzy controller is applied to control the damping force of air suspension. In the fuzzy controller, the error and error change rate between desired value and feedback are adopted as the input variables, and the duty cycle of PWM is adopted as the output variable. A hardware-in-the-loop experiment platform is developed for the simulation analysis in the air suspension system. In order to facilitate the observation and analysis the system state in the simulation process, a simulation monitoring platform is designed with the help of dSPACE ControlDesk.

articleTitle: Item Recommendation via Latent Topic Tag
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Overwhelmed by the wide scope and variety of contents, users are facing difficult choices of selecting items. Semantics-based recommendation technology has recently received a lot of attention, since the new knowledge can be found through the semantic relation between items, which improved the content-based recommendation on user-item bipartite graphs. In this paper, we employ a hybrid method, using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA)to form the topic tag and using Higher-Order Singular Value Decomposition (HOSVD)to recommend items on user-tag-item tripartite graphs. The precision of our method outperforms the traditional collaborative filtering (CF)algorithm based on user-item bipartite graphs and Topic-Sensitive PageRank system (TSPR)algorithm based on user-tag-item tripartite graphs. In addition, the performance HOSVD achieve the best when extracting 60% core information from tensor. This work could be applied to mobile app platforms recommending top-l item for.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Sliding Mode Control of Discrete-Time Markov Jump Systems with Partially Unknown Transition Probabilities
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the issue of event-triggered sliding mode control for discrete-time Markov jump systems with partially unknown transition probabilities. The problems of information channel congestion are solved through the event-triggered scheme. By utilizing Lyapunov stability theory, sufficient conditions that ensure the sliding dynamics achieve the desired performance are derived. A new sliding mode control law is designed such that the reach ability, the stochastic stability and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</sub> performance are guaranteed simultaneously. Finally, a numerical example is proposed to show the effectiveness of the sliding mode control scheme.

articleTitle: Reliable Model Predictive Control for Linear Sampled-Data System with Input Constraints
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel model predective control algorithm is proposed. By discretizing the sampled-data system and transforming it into a polytopic uncertain system, a reliable model predictive controller is designed for the sampled-data system. Based on this transfer, a class of linear matrix inequalities is formulated as the sampled-data controller. Finally, a simulation of numerical example is presented to verify the result.

articleTitle: Leader-Following Consensus of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems Using Observer-Based Event-Triggered Control
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the problem of leader-following consensus for a class of multi-agent systems with Lipschitz nonlinear dynamics. For reducing the communication resources, the centralized and decentralized event-triggered consensus strategies are proposed, respectively. Then, in the view of graph theory and Lyapunov stability theory, the triggering function which is related to the states of neighbor agents and corresponding agent, is obtained. Finally, a simulation example is included to demonstrate the effectiveness of the control strategies.

articleTitle: Pattern Classification of Motor Imagery EEG-NIRS Based on SVM with Artificial Fish Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: To address the problems of parameter setting and the poor classification accuracy in the traditional support vector machine (SVM), this paper proposes an approach to optimize the penalty factor and kernel parameter of SVM classifier based on artificial fish swarm algorithm (AFSA). AFSA-SVM was applied in two-class pattern classification problem, and common spatial pattern (CSP) algorithm was employed to extract the features of motor imagery electroencephalogram (EEG) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) signals in this paper. The total classification accuracy of AFSA-SVM classifier was higher than that of traditional SVM classifier about 5 %. The method proposed could improve classification accuracy of SVM classifier and has its advantages.

articleTitle: Research Status of Robot Calibration Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Calibration plays an increasingly important role in the control of robots. This paper discusses the calibration of robots from the four steps of calibration: modeling, measurement, parameter identification and compensation. The study outlined the current work on robot calibration, proposed the deficiencies of the existing calibration technology and future development trends, in order to promote the further development and application of calibration technology for robotic systems.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Robust Spectral Clustering Approach for Subspace Classification
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Traditional low-rank representation (LRR)and variant algorithms based on LRR have been proved as effective methods for subspace clustering tasks in machine learning. However, the majority of the existing LRR-related algorithms relax the rank minimization problem by the trace norm minimization. It is rarely accurate to get the optimal solution guaranteed by the definition. Meanwhile, these methods can not well reveal the internal structure of the classification. In this paper, we propose an efficient and robust subspace clustering method to overcome these drawbacks. A robust self-representation coefficient matrix is learned by utilizing the Schatten- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> norm instead of the conventional rank function. Besides, the strongest block-diagonal structure of the coefficient representation matrix is enhanced by learning and optimizing the co-association matrix with the soft label of clustering results simultaneously in an unified framework. The affinity graphs constructed in this paper can clearly reveal the intrinsic structures of the data sets. Extensive experiments on the real data sets demonstrate that our novel proposed method can perform more effective than the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Analyzing Jobs-Housing Spatial Relationship Based on Floating Car Data
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In recent years, the increasingly fast urbanization process has led to the separation of jobs and residence locations in many cities which caused heavy traffic and air pollution. Various kinds of data are applied to analyze jobs-housing balance. This paper studied jobs-housing spatial relationship using floating car data by means of data mining in space grid scale and district scale. The results of clustering of floating car data were used to get the distribution of employment area and residential area in grid scale. The distribution of commuting distance and commuting time in both scales and the separation of job and residential place indicators in different district revealed the jobs-housing spatial characteristics comprehensively and quantitatively. The results show that this method can analyze the characteristics of jobs-housing spatial relationship quickly and finely based on the floating car data.

articleTitle: Power Optimization Based on Successive Convex Approximation in Smart Grid Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the successive convex approximation algorithm (SCAA)to solve the non-linear and non-convex power optimization problem in smart grid communications. The SCAA can effectively converge to the convex solution of power optimization and reduce the co-tier interferences among demand-side communication networks. Simulation results demonstrate that the SCAA has a fast convergence speed and improve the transmission rate of the whole network.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural-Based Tracking Design of Stochastic Switched Systems with Saturation
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this article, a novel adaptive neural tracking controller is constructed for a type of nonstrict-feedback stochastic nonlinear switched systems with saturation. In the design algorithm, an auxiliary signal is introduced such that the design difficulties caused by input saturation is handled, the variable separation technology is adopted to deal with the problem of the nonstrict-feedback structure, and the desired common Lyapunov function is constructed via backstepping. Finally, stability analysis proves that the control target is achieved.

articleTitle: Ensemble Based Quantification for 18O Labeled LC-MS
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: With the development of machine learning, researchers can get more accurate results for bioinformatics by using complex machine learning methods. However, these complex machine learning methods are always time consuming and computationally expensive. On the other hand, the methods like boosting in classification can be considered for those traditional “weak” methods to get better performance. By combining simple regression approaches, an ensemble based method is proposed in this paper for <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup>O labeled LC-MS. Experimental results show that this proposed method is capable for better quantification results.

articleTitle: Mean Square Asymptotic Stability for Stochastic Genetic Regulatory Networks with Interval Time-Varying Delays
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, we study the stability analysis of stochastic genetic regulatory networks with interval time-varying delays. At first, we develop a new inequality to deal with multiple integrals with stochastic terms. Then, based on the suitable Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional and linear matrix inequalities, a delay-dependent and delay-rate-dependent mean square asymptotic stability criterion is derived. Finally, it is shown that the proposed method is effective and feasible through a numerical example.

articleTitle: Stabilizing Switching Control for DC- DC Converter in Two-Stage Photovoltaic Grid Connected Inverters
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In photovoltaic system, the maximum power point tracking technology (MPPT)makes the input voltage and current of the pre-stage DC-DC converter in a two-stage grid connected inverter variable because of external factors such as light and temperature. In order to improve the stability of pre-stage boost converter under variable input, a switching liner parameter varying (LPV)model of boost converter is established. Based on the established model, a stable switching signal of boost converter is derived from Lyapunov stability criterion of nonlinear stability analysis. Then a new control strategy of boost converter is designed by the switching signal. Based on the bifurcation theory, the stability of the control model is analyzed. The results show that the control strategy can make the boost converter output the voltage with less ripple, and the analysis of a series of bifurcation diagrams shows that the boost converter will not be unstable under the control strategy. Finally, the theoretical results are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Formation-Containment Control for Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The fixed-time formation-containment control is studied for multi-agent systems with single-integrator dynamics in this paper. To be specific, the positions of leaders are required to realize the expected formation and the positions of followers are designed to enter the convex hull formed by the leaders at the same time. With the neighboring condition information, the protocols are designed for both time-invariant and time-varying formation cases to realize the fixed-time formation-containment. Then for the two cases, the multi-agent system can simultaneously realize the prescribed formation and containment performance within a prescribed settling time that is regardless of initial conditions, which is demonstrated by mathematical deduction. Simulations are included to prove the effectiveness of our control protocols.

articleTitle: Reliable H∞ Filtering for Discrete-Time Takagi-Sugeno Fuzzy Markov Jump Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of reliable H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> filtering for discrete-time Takagi -Sugeno fuzzy nonhomogeneous Markov jump systems with the sensor fault matrix known and unknown, which time-varying transition probability matrix is depicted as a convex polytope set. Based on a parameter-dependent, fuzzy-basis-dependent and mode-dependent Lyapunov function, sufficient conditions are shown to guarantee that the filtering error system is stochastically stable and satisfies a H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance index. Finally, simulation results by a numerical example illustrates efficiency of new proposed methods.

articleTitle: Dissipative Filtering of Singular Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Singular Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The problem of fuzzy dissipative control for discrete-time interval type-2 fuzzy singular system is investigated in this paper. The full-order interval type-2 fuzzy filters are designed with the uncertain terms in premise rules and membership functions. Firstly, based on the Lyapunov stability theory, the interval type-2 fuzzy filter error system is proved to be admissible and strictly dissipative. Secondly, the the derived condition of the interval type-2 fuzzy filter can be converted into linear matrix inequalities. Finally, a numerical example is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Image Encryption Based on Fully Phase Encoding and Pixel Scrambling in Gyrator Transform Domain
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel optical image encryption scheme using fully phase encoding and pixel scrambling techniques in gyrator transform domain. The primary image will be firstly scrambled using chaotic cat map, and then encoded into a phase-only complex function. Finally, the complex data will be transformed into gyrator transform domain. An iterative structure is designed for security enhancement of the cryptosystem. In the proposed cryptosystem, control parameters of the chaotic map and rotation angle of gyrator transform serve as the secret keys. Numerical simulations and security analyses demonstrate the high security performance and noise resistance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: The Design of PID Controller Based on Improved Bird Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The proportional - integral - derivative(PID)controller has been widely employed in industrial control systems. However, the PID parameters obtained by Ziegler-Nichols(Z-N)method are difficult to show superior performance. Based on the improved bird swarm algorithm(IBSA), a method of parameter optimization of PID controller is proposed in this paper. We improve the three parameters ω, C and S respectively. The ω is the inertia coefficient added to the bird swarm algorithm(BSA). The C and S are cognitive coefficient and social coefficient of BSA respectively. In addition, the PID controller using IBSA is also called IBSA-PID controller. In order to validate the superiority of IBSA, we compare IBSA with particle swarm optimization(PSO), genetic algorithm(GA)and bird swarm algorithm(BSA)under the aid of integrated time and absolute error(ITAE). Experimental results validate that IBSA has superior performance than other algorithms on the aspect of convergence, robust, and time cost.

articleTitle: Maritime Traffic Safety Assessment in Restricted Visibility
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, a safety assessment model is proposed for maritime traffic in restricted visibility. Based on fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method, the mathematical models which consider the safety characteristics of maritime traffic are presented. Then risk matrix is developed by using fuzzy information distribution method to correct the risk matrix established by empirical investigation method. By establishing risk matrix of maritime traffic in restricted visibility, the maritime traffic safety level can be evaluated precisely and the maritime traffic safety risk pre-assessment system could be developed in the future.

articleTitle: Robust Tracking Control for Small Unmanned Helicopter
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The small unmanned helicopter is a strongly coupling system which has a small size, and it is very sensitive to external disturbance. Therefore, it is very meaningful to study the robust control of small unmanned helicopter. In this paper, the dynamic response is represent by linear model of hover flight mode. In order to make the angle rate of the small unmanned helicopter to track the desired angle rate, extended state observer is designed to observe the states and disturbances of small unmanned helicopter which are immeasurable. Then, for the input disturbance, it is offset by observed value, and for the system disturbance, a robust tracking controller is designed to suppress it. Finally, the robust tracking performance of the controller is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Adaptive Pitch-Axis Control for an AUV Based on Characteristic Modeling Method
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Characteristic modeling is an effective engineering method for the control design, which has many successful applications in the military and civilian fields. In this paper, this technique is applied to the pitch-axis motion control of an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV). A characteristic model of the pitch dynamics of the AUV is established with its parameters identified on-line. Then, An adaptive controller is designed based on the obtained model, which consists of feedforward tracking control, golden-section adaptive control, differential control and integral control. Finally, the validity and accuracy of the controller are verified by several simulation results.

articleTitle: Study on Fault Diagnosis Method of Emulsifier Based on Empirical Wavelet Transform and SVM
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: For the problem that the signals measured in the fault diagnosis of the emulsifier are non-stationary, non-linear signals and contain a large amount of background noise. This paper presents an emulsifier fault diagnosis method based on empirical wavelet transform (EWT) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). Empirical wavelet transform is a new adaptive signal decomposition method, which inherits the respective advantages of Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) and wavelet analysis methods. By extracting frequency domain maximum points to adaptively split the Fourier spectrum to separate different modalities. Then, a band-pass filter bank is adaptively constructed in the frequency domain to construct an orthogonal wavelet function to extract an AM-FM component with a Compact Support Fourier spectrum to better extract fault features. At the same time combining the advantages of SVM in small sample classification and identification, a fault diagnosis model based on EWT and SVM is proposed. The experimental results show that this method can extract the rotor rub-impact fault characteristics better. Compared with the EMD method, the improved EWT algorithm is better.

articleTitle: Exponential Synchronization of Chaotic Lur'e Systems via Event-Triggered Control
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This study deals with the synchronization problem for master-slave chaotic Lur'e systems (CLS). In order to reduce the communication burden, a novel adaptive event-triggered control (ETC)mechanism is developed. Different from the existing event-triggered schemes, the parameter of the event-trigger in this paper is adaptively adjusted. Moreover, the proposed event-triggered scheme exploits the advantage of the continuous-time measurements and ensures a minimum inter-event time. A special Lyapunov functional is employed to reduce the conservative of the synchronization criterion. Correspondingly, the desired event-triggered parameters are obtained by a linear matrix inequalities (LMIs)approach. Simulation results of Chua's circuit is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed techniques.

articleTitle: A Model-Free Design for Tracking Control of Nonholonomic Mobile Robots Under Polar Coordinates
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel model-free design method under polar coordinates space for the tracking problem of nonholonomic mobile robots. The proposed tracking controllers to track nonholonomic mobile robots without any prior knowledge of the robot model. It drives the tracking error to the predetermined neighborhood of zero with information which is not complete.

articleTitle: Low-Complexity Adaptive Control for Unknown Pure Feedback Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this work, an adaptive control technique is proposed for a category of unknown pure feedback nonlinear systems by using back-stepping technique. To guarantee the low-complexity of controller, a novel back-stepping control scheme is developed to solve the problems of unknown nonlinearities and “explosion of complexity” by integrating the mean value theorem and supremum norm theory with first-order sliding-mode differentiator, which can guarantee that the number of adjustable parameters is only one and the design is an approximation-free control scheme. The developed adaptive controller guarantees that all signals in the closed-loop system are bounded and the system output eventually converges to a small neighborhood of the desired reference signal. Finally, Simulation results further demonstrate the validity of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Further Improved Wirtinger Inequalities Approach to Stability of Systems with Time-Varying Delays
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper develops a further improved Wirtinger inequality to derive stability condition of time-varying-delay systems based on an approximate inequality. Then, applying the inequality to three class of systems with time-varying-delay, some original delay-dependent criteria is obtained by utilizing Lyapunov- Krasovskii functional. The analysis shows that the new inequality can further reduce the conservativeness compared to other methods. Moreover, the further improved Wirtinger inequality achieves a high-order approximation. Finally, some numerical examples are given to illuminate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Improved Calculation Method for Short Circuit Current of Marine Power System
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, an improved method is proposed for calculating the short circuit current of marine power systems. Seven typical algorithms were compared and the China Classification Society (CCS) algorithm was researched. Compared with the original CCS algorithm which ignores the influence of the external impedance when calculating the steady-state short circuit current, the resistance and reactance of the cable from the generator to the main switchboard were fully considered in the improved calculation method. The calculation result from the combined programming shows that when the length of the cable is changed, the accuracy of the short circuit current is improved by the new calculation method.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification Method for Quad-Rotor UAV Based on the Lyapunov-MARI Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The traditional parameter identification method of the quad-rotor UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) model requires special experimental equipment, and the experimental process is very complex. To overcome this problem, the current paper proposes a Lyapunov-MARI (Model Reference Adaptive Identification) algorithm, which only needs the UAV and some common sensors to realize the parameter identification. Firstly, the current paper determines specific parameters which are not easy to be measured in the quad-rotor UAV model. These parameters mainly include the three axis moments of inertia, the rotors lift coefficient and drag coefficient. Then, for the moments of inertia, the traditional period measurement method of the Rope Suspension Approach is improved. For the lift and drag coefficients, the Lyapunov-MARI algorithm is proposed for the parameter identification. The result shows that the flight state calculated by the identified parameters are compatible with the actual flight data.

articleTitle: Investigation of State Convergence Issues on Uncertain Perturbed Nonlinear T-S Fuzzy System
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper addresses the state convergence problems on nonlinear perturbed T-S fuzzy system with uncertainties. The recently developed delay division method using geometric sequence is combined with a new integral delay-partitioning approach to overcome the negative effects of the mixed time delays. Then a modified Lyapunov Krasovskii functional (LKF) using flexible integral intervals is established. This development can reduce the computation burden and also improve the efficiency for obtaining the expected delay upper bound.

articleTitle: The Simulation and Synchronous Control of the Hyperchaotic Couette-Taylor Flow System
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper presents a four-dimensional hyperchaotic Couette-Taylor flow system and exhibits hyperchaotic attractors of the new hyperchaotic system. We discussed the global exponential attraction set and positive invariant set of the system. The adaptive control for the hyperchaotic Couette-Taylor flow system's synchronization with time delay via a single variable is achieved. Numerical simulation results shows the method is effective.

articleTitle: Flying Inverted Pendulum
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper propose the use of a cascade control method for the inverted pendulum design problem with quadro-tor as the experimental platform, which mainly uses the imu information of the quadrotor and the OptiTrack motion capture system to capture the position information of the inverted pendulum as the system feedback, and form a closed-loop control, the feasibility of the simulation verification method on matlab, and finally achieve the balance effect of the inverted pendulum on the quadrotor in a physical experiment.

articleTitle: Novel Delay-Dependent H∞ Synchronization of Chaotic Lur'e Systems with Time-Varying Delays Based on Sampled-Data Control
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper investigates the problems of H∞synchronization of master-slave Lur’ e systems with uncertainty parameters and variable samplings using sampled-data control. By developing some new terms, we construct a new piecewise time-dependent Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) to fully make ues of the available sampling information of the chaotic system and the available features of the nonlinear function vector. Furthermore, some of the symmetric matrices mentioned in LKF are not requested to be positive definite. Based on the LKF and Free-Matrix-Based (FMB) integral inequality, several less conservative synchronization criteria are derived to achieve the asymptotic synchronization of the master-slave system with a guaranteed H∞norm bound. The desired sampled-data controller which ensures the stability of the error system and declines negative effects of external disturbance on the basis of H∞norm bound can be achieved by solving a set of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) with the maximal allowable upper bound of sampling. Finally, a numerical simulation of the Chua's circuit is considered and solved by the proposed approach so as to show the benefits and the superiority of the proposed approach over some existing methods.

articleTitle: High-Precision PMU Testing Device Based on Synchronous Clock Source
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: As the lack of on-spot testing equipment for synchronous Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU), the on-spot testing work of PMU has not been carried out effectively. So the function of Wide area measurement system (W AMS)based on PMU was restricted greatly. In the on-spot PMU testing, the major issues are the implement of the power angle measurement and sufficient dynamic-precision. To solve these problems, we developed a high-precision PMU testing device based on the synchronous clock source in this paper. The proposed device can output amplitude, phase, frequency and low frequency vibrator of signals, which also synchronize with the second pulse of Global Positioning System (GPS). We further constructed the synchronous simulated system by the PMU testing device we developed, which is used for implementing the test on the spot. It is effective not only for static precision, but also for dynamic precision and functions of PMU.

articleTitle: Distributed Consensus Control for Second-Order Stochastic Nonlinear Multiagent Systems Using Command Filter Backstepping
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The issue of distributed consensus control for second-order stochastic nonlinear multiagent systems is considered. By using command filter backstepping approach, a distributed controller is designed. Semi-globally uniformly ultimately boundedness (SGUUB) in probability of all signals has been proved in the closed-loop networked systems, and the consensus errors have converged to a neighbourhood of original point. To verify the validity of developed algorithm, a numerical example is provided.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Fault Accommodation of Uncertain Complex Dynamical Networks with Nonlinear Couplings
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper is considered with the adaptive fault accommodation problem for the uncertain complex networks with unknown fault and nonlinear couplings. It is assumed that the topology structure and coupling strength are all unknown. By combining the graph theory approach, the fuzzy logic theory and the adaptive method, a new adaptive fuzzy fault accommodation controller is constructed to ensure that the effect of the unknown fault and the system uncertainty can be eliminated completely. Furthermore, it is shown that the synchronization error of the networks can converge asymptotically to zero. Finally, one Chua's circuit example is given to illustrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fast Nonsingular Terminal Sliding Mode Control for Near Space Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This work studies fast nonsingular terminal sliding mode (FNTSM)attitude tracking control scheme for near space vehicle in presence of unknown compound disturbances. An adaptive law is presented to compensate the effect of disturbance. In addition, a FNTSM controller is proposed to drive tracking errors to zero in finite time. Next, the finite-time convergence of sliding mode variable and tracking error is proved. Finally, a simulation illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Adaptive Consensus Tracking Control for Multi-Agent Systems with Network Communication Failures
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper is concerned with the adaptive consensus tracking control problem for multi-agent systems subject to intermittent communication failures. Based only on the state information of neighboring agents, a new tracking control strategy is designed by applying distributed adaptive technique. Also, by employing the multiple Lyapunov functions approach and algebraic graph theory, the tracking protocol design is given in terms of linear matrix inequalities. The novelty of this paper is that the presented adaptive consensus protocol has no requirement of the global information of the network topology. Furthermore, it is proved that the states of the tracking error system are uniformly ultimately bounded. Finally, the effectiveness of the presented distributed adaptive control strategy is illustrated with a simulated example.

articleTitle: Type-2 Fuzzy Forecasting of Main Road Traffic Flow
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In the process of development of modern intelligent transportation system, how to effectively deal with the non-linear, time-varying and sudden traffic flow data and accurately predict the traffic flow is one of the important technologies to achieve traffic control and guidance. Now most of the methods are through the shallow model in learning, it is to easy to fall into the local extreme phenomenon which can not be more complex mathematical operations. In order to overcome the limitation of the traditional forecasting technology on the random variation of the massive traffic flow data, this paper proposes a traffic flow forecasting method based on the interval type-2 fuzzy sets. Firstly, stratified sampling and K-means clustering are combined to collect the data of the roads in all directions of the main road. The central limit theorem is used to convert the scattered data points into the interval form first, and the fuzzy set and type-2 fuzzy set, and through fuzzy to get the forecast result finally. The experimental results show that the result obtained in this paper is a range of forecasting region, which is difficult to be achieved by traditional methods and has high accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Ship Course Keeping Controller Design with General Noise
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, a new model of ship heading control with general noise is established to model the noise perturbations in the ship course keeping nonlinear system accurately. General noise, which includes white and nonwhite noise, is introduced to the ship course second-order model which is described by random differential equations (RDEs). The controller is designed by incorporating backstepping and Lyapunov stability theory. The noise-to-state stability is analyzed and the asymptotical gain in probability can be obtained. The proposed method can remove some strong constraints of the concerned noisy system which is driven by white noise, where the white noise is viewed as the formal derivative of a Wiener process. Finally taking YUPENG ship of Dalian Maritime University as an example, the simulation is carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: New Result on Finite-Time Boundedness Analysis for Switched Linear Time-Delay Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper focuses on the finite-time boundedness of switched linear time-delay systems with exogenous disturbance. An improved Lyapunov function with a finite number of discontinuities is presented for each system mode. By utilizing the newly proposed Lyapunov function together with the average dwell time (ADT) characteristics, a sufficient criterion is established to guarantee the finite-time boundedness of the underlying switched system. Finally, a numerical example is provided to show the validity and superiority of the method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Indoor Localization for Mobile Robots Using Odometry and Vision System: A Pseudo Measurement Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper studies the problem of indoor localization for mobile robots using odometry and vision system. As the odometry adopts a higher sampling rate than the camera, a pseudo measurement approach is proposed to recover the visual measurements such that the position of the mobile robot can be estimated by the visual measurements with the same sampling rate of the odometry. To improve the robustness with respect to measurement variations, a self-tuning parameter is introduced in the pseudo measurement and the normalized least mean square algorithm is used to adjust the self-tuning parameter adaptively. By formulating the localization problem in the framework of Bayesian estimation, the unscented Kalman filter is utilized to handle the nonlinear filtering problem. Experimental results are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Model of Optimal Iterative Learning Control for Distributed Parameter Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper suggests a data-driven model for distributed parameter systems, using iterative learning control with optimal index. First, a linear mapping from input to output of a continuous system is built, and after that the object function of the continuous system is given. Then, the continuous system is discretized by finite difference methods. Moreover, a dynamic leaner data-driven model is proposed, which is utilized when the coefficients of the system is unknown. Finally, the standard quadratic cost function of the discrete system is presented.

articleTitle: Global Exponential Stability and Stabilizing for Neural Networks with Time-Varying Delays and Impulses
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this note, the stabilizing for neural networks with time-varying delays and impulses are considered. By choosing proper Lyapunov functionals and differential inequality techniques with delay and impulse, the sufficient conditions for the globally impulsively exponential stable and exponentially stabilized via an impulsive controller are obtained. An example is given to prove the correctness of our theory.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Consensus for Multi-Agent Systems with Impulsive Effect
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The paper primarily investigates the fixed-time consensus problem of multi-agent systems (MAS) with impulsive effect. We firstly present a novel and suitable fixed-time protocol to solve the fixed-time consensus problems of MAS with impulsive effect. Under the control protocol, it is theoretically demonstrated that fixed-time consensus of MAS could be legitimately solved. Finally, some numerical simulations are given to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: On Learning Law Design of Fuzzy Hopfield Neural Networks with Time-Varying Delay
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The stability of a class of fuzzy neural networks is studied in this paper. A fuzzy Lyapunov function is proposed, based on which, the learning law of the weighting matrices are designed to guarantee the system to be passive. A numerical example is given to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Improved Distributed Cooperative Filters for Minimum-Variance Unbiased Estimation of Unknown Inputs and States in Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The estimation of unknown inputs and states is important for multi-agent systems. In this study, we propose an improved filter that overcomes the shortcomings of the existing filter. This filter estimate the unknown inputs in cooperative mode and the states in decentralized mode, respectively. Compared with the former one, the improved filters not only could reduce the amount of information transmitted and calculated, but also have better estimation performance. The optimal gain matrix of the proposed filters is derived and the effectiveness of the filters is shown through simulation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Tracking Control for Robotic Manipulators with Time-Varying State Constraints
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The problem of adaptive neural control is mainly addressed for the robotic manipulators with time-varying full state constraints and dead-zone in this paper, which can ensure the desired performance in a finite time. In order to overcome the problems of the time-varying state constraints, the time-varying barrier Lyapunov functions (TVBLFs)are adopted to insure that all the states are not violated from the predetermined range. Moreover, by employing the backstepping procedure and Lyapunov stability theory, the system stability and desired performance are guaranteed in finite time. Finally, the effectiveness of the devised approach is proved via some simulation results.

articleTitle: Approximation-Based Asymptotical Tracking Control of Nonlinear Systems Quantized Actuator
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive fuzzy asymptotical quantized tracking controller is presented for nonlinear systems with unmodeled dynamics and non-lower triangular form. The dynamic signal technique is applied to handle the difficulty from unmodeled dynamics, and fuzzy systems are used to estimate the uncertain nonlinear functions. By using backstepping technique, an adaptive fuzzy asymptotical quantized tracking control scheme is proposed. With the help of Lyapunov theory, the semi-globally uniformly ultimate boundedness of all closed-loop system signals and asymptotical tracking performance are guaranteed. Simulations illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: An Effective Two-Stage Feature Selection Method with Parameters Optimized by Simulated Annealing Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: With the increase of the dimension of the collected data, the research of feature selection has gained more and more attention in recent years. As an essential preprocessing method, feature selection can not only reduce the cost of modeling by deleting those unnecessary features, but also improve the precision of the model in some degree. In this paper, an effective feature selection method is proposed, which is based on Mutual Information and Cosine Distance with parameters optimized by Simulated Annealing algorithm (MICD-SA). The proposed method achieves the goal of dimension reduction through two-stage feature selection operations. First, features are selected based on the mutual information between features and labels. Then, cosine distance between each feature is introduced to further reduce the redundancy of the selected features in stage one. Finally, the simulated annealing algorithm is adopted to automatically optimize the two thresholds used in the previous two-stage feature selection process. In addition, the proposed method is also applied to four high dimensional datasets to test its feasibility and effectiveness. Three feature selection methods combined with four different classifiers (KNN, CART, SVM, NB)are tested and their results are compared. The proposed method's effectiveness both in accuracy and feature number are well proved by the comparison.

articleTitle: Constructions of Strict Lyapunov Functions for Homogeneous Time-Varying Systems with Applications in Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: We provide a new technique for constructing strict Lyapunov functions (CSLFs) for time-varying systems. The definition of homogeneous auxiliary system is given, where it is assumed that certain homogeneous functions are admitted with their derivatives, in terms of the error systems, bounded by periodic functions. Based on the homogeneous auxiliary system, sufficient conditions of uniform asymptotical stability for time-varying systems are formulated. Unlike classical CSLFs, where non-strict Lyapunov functions or persistency of excitation condition are required, our criterion is greatly relaxed for broad classes of systems. The utility of our result is illustrated through the well-known consensus problem of multi-agent systems.

articleTitle: Big-Data Analysis of Multi-Source Logs for Network Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: In this paper, a Spark-based big data cluster is built to analyze the large-scale multi-source log data and to detect computer and network abnormal behaviors. By developing and assembling data mining, machine learning, and statistical analysis technologies, the large-scale log data can be quickly analyzed, and the abnormal attack behaviors can be accurately recognized.

articleTitle: Robust Laser Radar-Based Robot Localization Using UFIR Filtering
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: The indoor robot localization becomes more and more important since the indoor robot has been widely used in our life. And the laser radar is one of the most widely used example due to its high accuracy and easy installation. In this paper, unbiased finite impulse response (UFIR)filter is employed to fusion the laser measurement, which can improve the robustness of the robot localization. The real test for the comparison of Kalman filter (KF)and UFIR filter is done to show the robustness of the UFIR filter.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Sliding Mode Control for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: This paper proposes a T -S fuzzy model-based sliding mode control for permanent magnet synchronous motors(PMSM). Firstly, the PMSM is modeled as a T-S fuzzy singularly perturbed system(SPS). Secondly, the parameter perturbations and local torque changes are taken into account in the design of T-S fuzzy model-based sliding mode controller. In order to reduce the chattering problem, the fuzzy control method is used to replace the discontinuous sliding mode controller. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed methods are demonstrated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Memristive Neural Network Based Reinforcement Learning with Reward Shaping for Path Finding
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Robot is becoming an important role in people's daily life and work. Especially, in some extreme circumstances, robots can be used for searching and rescuing to improve the rescue efficiency and decrease additional casualties. Reinforcement learning, especially q-learning, is always employed in robot path finding for the unknown environment. However, the basic reinforcement learning always faces the problem of inefficiency and blindness. In this paper, a novel path finding method called MRNS q-learning is proposed. By leveraging the advantages of the reward shaping q-learning and memristive RBF neural network, this method may provide higher processing efficiency and convergence speed. In addition, a hardware architecture for the MRNS q-learning is also given. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and ascendancy of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Reward Mechanism for Block Mining in PoW-Based Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2018 5th International Conference on Information, Cybernetics, and Computational Social Systems (ICCSS)
abstract: Blockchain brings a peer-to-peer transaction solution without a trusted third authority over the peer-to-peer network. Proof-of-work (PoW), also called `mining', incents some peers (called miners)to compete for the right of block generation by rewarding a certain mount of cryptocurrency. Hence, PoW undertakes the cryptocurrency creation and block generation in a blockchain based transaction system (BTS). However, in a BTS, the block mining reward (BMR)will be terminated after that the regulated quantity of currency have been minted. Although the voluntarily paid transaction fee is allowed to support BMR, the stable reward for block mining is no longer guaranteed, and which inevitably destroys the sustainability of BTS. In this work, we propose a sustainable reward mechanism (SRM)for block mining in BTS. Specifically, SRM introduces a mandatory transaction fee mechanism with dedicated fee rate determination algorithm.
